title: Pattern Recognition Drill: Which Technique Is This?
oneLiner: Read a problem in plain English and name the technique -- no code, just the reflex that decides whether you freeze in an interview.
keyTakeaway: Most of the difficulty in an unfamiliar problem is choosing the approach, not writing it. Problems announce their technique through small phrases -- "sorted", "contiguous", "in O(1) per query", "minimum value that still works", "all possible" -- and this drill trains you to spot those phrases without writing a line of code.
explanation:
Every Patterns lesson ends with you writing the solution -- but in a real interview, nobody tells you which pattern the problem is. Recognizing it is its own skill, and it's much faster to practice on its own than by fully solving problems. This drill gives you a problem statement and asks which technique fits; no editor, no test cases.

After each answer you see the signal phrases that gave it away and the technique it's most often confused with. Skim those as carefully as the answer -- they're the portable part. The same trigger words show up again in problems you've never seen.

Your score and the techniques you keep missing are tracked for this session, so a second run can focus on the weak spots.
